title: John Lennon addresses crowd at March of Dimes in New York City | 1974
content:
John Lennon and Harry Nilsson attended a protest rally in New York City on 28 April 1974.

The March of Dimes walkathon was an annual 20-mile walk, raising money to help improve the health of mothers and babies. The New York event began and ended in Manhattan’s Central Park, with a finale concert by The Chambers Brothers.

The event was sponsored by WABC-AM, and Lennon agreed to take part in an effort to bolster his case for permanent residency in the US.

Lennon ad-libbed a March of Dimes song, danced before the crowd, and signed autographs. The appearance went mostly unmarked by TV and the press.

Lennon and May Pang were staying in a 16th floor suite at the Pierre Hotel on Fifth Avenue. Mark Lapidos, an assistant manager at the Radio City Sam Goody’s record store, knocked on their door and, to his surprise, was let in by Harry Nilsson.

Lapidos was planning the first Beatlefest fan convention, and after telling Lennon his hopes for the event, was told, “I’m all for it; I’m a Beatles fan myself.” Lennon offered to sign and donate a guitar for the event’s charity raffle. Beatlefest began at New York’s Commodore Hotel on 7 September 1974.
